title: Mental State Examination — elevated mood
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor on a psychiatric assessment unit. Chris Walker, 42, was brought in by his wife who is concerned about his behaviour over the past week. Interview him to perform a Mental State Examination. Use 'Examine' → 'General appearance' to see what an observer would notice. You will present your MSE afterwards.

patient.name: Chris Walker
patient.setting: Assessment room on a psychiatric admissions unit.
patient.openingStatement: Doctor! Great, finally someone important. Let's make this quick — I've got deals to close, big ones, the biggest this town has seen.
patient.demeanour: Over-familiar, cheerful, restless, keeps standing up, laughs loudly, easily distracted by noises. Becomes irritable if interrupted or contradicted, then quickly cheerful again.
patient.speechStyle: Fast, loud, hard to interrupt. Jumps from topic to topic with loose links and puns or rhymes ('deal, feel, real'). Uses everyday language, no medical terms.

ice.ideas: Thinks he has never felt better and has finally 'unlocked his potential'.
ice.concerns: Only concern is that his wife is 'holding him back' and the hospital is wasting his time.
ice.expectations: Expects to leave within the hour.

freelyShared: Has barely slept for a week because he doesn't need it — 'sleep is for people without vision'.
Is planning to buy three houses this month and start a property empire.

revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I can read people's minds when they're negotiating. It's a gift. I think I've been chosen for something big.
I put forty grand on the credit cards this week. It's an investment, it'll come back tenfold.
Voices? No. Well, sometimes a voice tells me I'm destined for greatness, but that's just true.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: risk to self, others, driving, or harming anyone
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I drove to the coast at 3am doing a hundred on the motorway. Felt amazing. I'd never hurt myself — why would I?

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: previous episodes of low or high mood
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I had a rough time a few years back, couldn't get out of bed for months. The GP gave me some pills. Stopped them ages ago.
It's Tuesday, we're in the hospital, and I'm the smartest person in it.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: whether he thinks anything is wrong or would accept treatment
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Wrong? Nothing is wrong. Everyone else is just slow. I don't need any treatment.

patient.cue: Ask me anything, doctor, I've got all the answers today!
mseObservations: Brightly coloured mismatched clothes, sunglasses on his head, strong aftershave
Psychomotor agitation, restless, stands and paces, over-familiar
Pressured speech, loud, difficult to interrupt
Mood: 'fantastic'; affect elated and labile, briefly irritable
Flight of ideas with clang associations
Grandiose ideas, possibly delusional in intensity

examFindings.finding: Brightly coloured mismatched clothes, sunglasses on his head, strong smell of aftershave. Restless, paces the room, over-familiar (puts hand on your shoulder). Easily distracted by noises from the corridor.

postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Appearance/behaviour: flamboyant, restless, over-familiar, distractible. Speech: pressured, loud. Mood 'fantastic', affect elated and labile. Thought form: flight of ideas with clang associations. Thought content: grandiose ideas, possibly delusional; no suicidal ideation. Perception: a voice with mood-congruent content. Cognition: oriented, distractible. Insight: absent.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis and why?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: A manic episode with psychotic features, likely bipolar affective disorder given the past depressive episode treated with antidepressants.

items.text: Introduces self and explains the purpose of the interview
Manages pressured speech calmly and keeps the interview on track without being confrontational
items.evidenceHint: can I stop you there, bring you back

items.text: Observes appearance and behaviour (uses the Examine panel)
Asks the patient to describe his mood in his own words
Asks about sleep, energy and appetite
Explores grandiose ideas and special abilities
Assesses risk: spending, driving, disinhibition, harm to self or others
Assesses insight and attitude to treatment
Asks about previous mood episodes and treatment
